neighbours.label: a possessive pronoun ('my', also 'their') in devotional or lyrical address, as in psalms and hymns ('my rock, my fortress'), as against the same pronoun in everyday prose
fire: Praise the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits.
Truly he alone is my refuge, my rock, and my salvation; I shall not be shaken.
O God, you are my God; early will I seek you, for my soul thirsts for you.
Sing to him a new song: the Lord is my light and my song forever.
In you, O Lord, I put my trust; let me never be put to shame.
Unto thee I lift up my eyes, O thou that dwellest in the heavens.
Be thou my vision, O Lord of my heart, my treasure, my best thought by day.
Lead me, O Lord, for you are my hope and my strength in the time of trouble.
quiet: After lunch I washed my car and then took my dog for a walk.
Yesterday I lost my wallet somewhere between the office and the bus stop.
Can you send me the file? My laptop crashed and I lost my notes.
Last week I finally repainted my bedroom a pale shade of blue.
Praise the Lord, all people, and forget not the benefits of the Lord.
Truly the Lord alone is a refuge, a rock, and a salvation to the faithful.
Sing to the Lord a new song, for the Lord is light and song forever.
Lead the people, O Lord, for you are the hope and the strength of the nation.
